analysis: Benign prostatic hypertrophy is a common condition in older men characterized by non-cancerous growth of the prostate gland. It can lead to urinary symptoms due to the enlarged prostate pressing on the urethra. While it can cause increases in PSA levels, it is not considered a precancerous lesion. Abdominal ultrasound is indeed a non-invasive method to assess prostate size and post-voiding residual. Rectal examination can help estimate prostate size. Treatment with 5-alpha reductase inhibitors can help decrease symptoms by reducing the size of the prostate gland. Therefore, the statement 'It is a precancerous lesion' is NOT true.
